claim: In a retrospective 11-centre cohort of 234 patients treated with LITT for mesial TLE, 58.0% achieved Engel I outcomes at both 1 and 2 years; more anterior/medial/inferior ablations including greater amygdala volume were associated with Engel I.

bibliographic_record.authors: Wu C, Jermakowicz WJ, Chakravorti S, Cajigas I, Sharan AD, et al.
bibliographic_record.title: Effects of surgical targeting in laser interstitial thermal therapy for mesial temporal lobe epilepsy: A multicenter study of 234 patients

supporting_passage: At both 1 and 2 years after LITT, 58.0% achieved Engel I outcomes.
passage_location: Abstract, Results section. Abstract only (full text not read). Europe PMC REST API (resultType=core, abstractText) for PMID 31112302; https://europepmc.org/abstract/MED/31112302; accessed 2026-11-01

population_and_design.population: mesial temporal lobe epilepsy treated with MR-guided LITT (age range not_reported in abstract)

endpoint.follow_up: 1 and 2 years after LITT (n analysed at each time point not_reported in abstract)
endpoint.predictors: history of bilateral tonic-clonic seizures decreased chance of Engel I; radiographic hippocampal sclerosis not associated

reported_observation: 58.0% Engel I at 1 and 2 years; ablation location (anterior, medial, inferior; amygdala) associated with Engel I.
author_inference: LITT is viable for properly evaluated mTLE; ablations should prioritise amygdala plus hippocampal head, parahippocampal gyrus and rhinal cortices.
contradictions: Unlike Gross 2018 (Emory) and Chen 2023 IPD-MA, radiographic hippocampal sclerosis was not associated with seizure outcome here.
overlap_note: Several contributing centres (e.g. Jefferson, Miami, Columbia) are also SLATE sites; patient overlap with SLATE and with single-centre LITT series is possible (to_verify). Likely pooled in later LITT meta-analyses.
